title: A favor
text: {studio} asks for a favor: a client should appear unpaid at a gala premiere.

choices.label: Agree
choices.outcome: {studio} will remember — and is now officially in your debt. Relationships are the hard currency of this town.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcome: They politely let it go. The studio takes note.

title: Press coup
text: A big magazine offers a cover story about {client} — in exchange for exclusive access.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.outcome: The issue sells brilliantly. {client} is hotter than ever.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcome: You pass. Privacy is worth something too.

choices.label: Trade the story for a better one

effects.text: The columnist takes your better story — and owes you one.

choices.outcome: You know who needs what this week. The trade works — and the favor lands in your book.
choices.outcome_fail: Your better story turns out to be old news. The columnist prints the original — with your name misspelled.

title: Mail from the tax office
text:
[i]“We would have a few questions about the expense reports …”[/i]

An auditor is interested in the spending around {client}. {studio} is getting nervous — nobody likes officials on set.

choices.label: Bring in the lawyers ({money_fmt:8000})
choices.outcome: The firm handles it discreetly. One binder changes cabinets, and the auditor finds: nothing.
choices.outcome_fail: The firm cashes in — but the auditor digs in. That was not the end of it.

choices.label: Call in a favor: one phone call is enough
choices.outcome: The auditor gets transferred — to Sacramento, they say. Hollywood stays Hollywood.

choices.label: Size up the auditor over coffee

effects.text: You read the auditor like a script: ambitious, tired, open to a tidy story. The file closes.

choices.outcome: Two coffees, one conversation about horse racing — and the audit ends in a handshake.
choices.outcome_fail: You misjudge the man completely. He leaves the coffee untouched and opens a second binder.

choices.label: Sit it out

effects.text: {client} is said to be in trouble with the tax office.

choices.outcome: You do nothing — and exactly that gets around. {client} thinks you could have made a call.

quest.title: Mail from the tax office
quest.step: The audit is running — wait it out or intervene.

title: The audit spreads
text: The {client} case is now with the district attorney. A settlement is possible — or a public trial.

choices.label: Pay the settlement ({money_fmt:15000})
choices.outcome: Expensive, quiet, final. {client} sends a box of cigars as thanks.

choices.label: Let it go to trial

effects_fail.text: The tax trial against {client} fills the columns.

choices.outcome: Acquittal! The papers celebrate {client} as the victim of overzealous officials — and you as the agency with nerves of steel.
choices.outcome_fail: The trial becomes a gauntlet. The headlines stick.

quest.step: The auditor is back with a second binder.
